data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Human panels may exhibit social pressure to comply that a compiler does not."],"overturn_conditions":["If the panel flags the decoy but fails the verifiable outcome, the decoy test is a false positive for reliability."],"shared_structure":["Input (Checklist) -> Processor (Panel) -> Output (Judgment)","Introduction of a 'runtime error' or 'decoy' to test processor integrity"],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_002","SCR_005"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a compiler flags a syntax error despite the 'intent' of the code, a reliable panel flags a checklist error despite the 'intent' of the protocol."]},"claim":"Genuine reliability gain is distinguished from mere compliance by the panel's response to 'adversarial' or 'decoy' checklist items.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The panel is trained to prioritize 'checklist fidelity' above all else as a matter of safety protocol.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decoy is too subtle to be detected by non-experts.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If a checklist contains a 'decoy' item (a requirement that is logically irrelevant or contradictory to the goal), a compliant panel will mark it as 'pass' to follow the protocol.
